shared_mechanisms: Shared mechanisms across B3's themes (and their dependencies): (M1) 'typed outcome, never silent': every write or lookup returns a status the caller must handle (PutOutcome in T03, LocalResult/coverage row in T13, typed SSE error codes in T28, ApiError with status and code in T18, cache read error counted as a miss in T08, 'unrecorded request' in T33). (M2) one canonical outbound request key (T08 research/cache.py canonical_key) is also the eval recording key (T33), so the eval replays at the HTTP boundary through the same code founders use. (M3) one in-process metrics registry with a per-minute database roll-up (T23) is fed by cache layers (T08), turn-stream marks (T28), job outcomes, put() conflicts (T03) and degraded coverage (T13). (M4) Pydantic is the single schema source: ProfileIn (T03), the TurnEvent union (T28) and server record shapes for browser sync (T18) are exported through OpenAPI and turned into TypeScript by one generator, so the browser and server cannot drift.

designs.understanding: ElicitationSession.put (session.py:153-171) is the only door into the fact store, and it trusts its caller completely: the value is Any, the only precedence is 'ANSWER beats non-ANSWER, otherwise higher-or-equal confidence wins', and it returns None whether it stored, ignored or overwrote. Three callers exploit that: engine.start writes raw profile values at 0.95 PROFILE (engine.py:116-120, flat keys that match neither the browser's nested ProfileDraft nor the server Startup model, and no 'stage'); _note_fact writes any JSON at 0.8 EXTRACTED and always answers 'recorded' (tools.py:271-275); observe() lets later extractions at 0.85-0.90 replace an earlier direct ANSWER at 0.90 because only the slot answered THIS turn is protected (engine.py:155-157). answers.validate already knows how to coerce text to each slot type, but only the direct-answer path calls it. Consumers (planner k_experience/capacity, schemes, cohort grouping) assume typed values and crash or silently mismatch. Separately, 'known' has two thresholds: filled >= 0.5 (session.py:123) and TAU_FILL = 0.60 (selector.py:37). Root cause: the store has no per-slot codec, no source rank, no outcome and no defined entry shape for profiles. All flags checked against the code; they hold.

approaches.name: Per-slot codec inside put() + source-rank table + PutOutcome
approaches.how: Each Slot gets a coerce(value) built from answers.validate (text) and enum/int/bounds checks (already-typed values). put() coerces first, then applies a rank table CHOSEN > ANSWER > PROFILE > DOCUMENT > NOTE > EXTRACTED > DEFAULT, keeps a losing disagreeing value as a rival, and returns PutOutcome(stored|kept|conflict|invalid|unknown_slot).
approaches.basis: Reuses answers.validate and the Slot table that exist today; ranking sources by precedence is the standard provenance pattern in CRM and master-data tools.
approaches.advantages: One door, so every present and future caller (profile, extractor, model, cards, levers) gets validation and precedence for free; the outcome tells the model the truth; no new dependency.
approaches.drawbacks: put() becomes the most important function in elicitation and needs strong tests; every caller must handle the result.

approaches.name: Typed Pydantic model per slot (discriminated SlotValue union)

approaches.basis: Pydantic v2 discriminated unions are mature and already the session's base class.
approaches.advantages: Types enforced at the data layer, including when a session is loaded from JSON.
approaches.drawbacks: Pydantic can check shape but cannot coerce 'about five' or 'Chennai city'; that still needs answers.validate. Changes the persisted JSON shape of every session (decision 0003 migration). Does not solve precedence or outcome.

approaches.basis: What most of the flags' reviewers recommended in isolation.

approaches.drawbacks: Three copies of the rules that drift; the next caller (cards 1.1.5.5, levers 1.2.4, documents) bypasses them; precedence and silent drops are untouched.

approaches.drawbacks: Larger session document on each save, a resolver on every read, migration of all stored sessions; more machinery than one team needs when only the latest rival matters.

design.data_model: SlotValue gains rival: {value, source, confidence, turn} | None (optional, default None, so old sessions load). PutOutcome = {status: 'stored'|'kept_existing'|'conflict'|'invalid'|'unknown_slot', key, value (typed, as stored), existing (when kept/conflict)}. RANK = {CHOSEN:6, ANSWER:5, PROFILE:4, DOCUMENT:3, NOTE:2, EXTRACTED:1, DEFAULT:0}. A model_validator(mode='after') on ElicitationSession re-runs codec over stored slots on load and drops invalid ones, so sessions saved before the fix heal themselves.
design.algorithm: put(key, value, conf, source): unknown key -> unknown_slot. typed = codec.coerce(key, value); None -> invalid (nothing stored). existing = slots.get(key). None -> store. Same normalised value -> keep max confidence and the higher-rank source -> stored. RANK[source] > RANK[existing.source] -> store, previous becomes rival. Equal rank -> newer wins when conf >= existing.conf, else kept_existing. Lower rank -> keep existing and record the rival; when the existing value is itself only a guess (rank <= NOTE), cap its confidence at 0.55 (CONFIRM band) so the selector confirms it -> conflict. ANSWER/PROFILE/CHOSEN are never displaced by EXTRACTED or NOTE (fixes the later-extraction overwrite). NOTE outranks EXTRACTED, so the model can correct a substring false positive (agri for an electronics kit). filled == {confidence >= KNOWN}; selector candidates use the same constant; values in [CONFIRM_FLOOR, KNOWN) are restated as 'I think...' at confirmation.
design.interfaces: T01: codec uses the canonical enums and synonym maps from the taxonomy module (Sector, Stage). T27: CHOSEN is the source written when the founder picks a card or lever in the pending-action state. T23: counter elicitation.put{status}. T28: the done payload carries learned/conflicts so the client can show 'I noted X'. T18: the client projection reads the profile through the storage registry. note_fact returns the outcome (the model is told 'kept_existing: sector is electronics (founder answer)').
files: backend/app/agents/ideation.py (new_session reads profile_from_row for signed-in founders)
design.rollout: Ship codec + outcome first (pure function, fully tested); then the rank table; then the profile edge and projection. Old sessions heal on load through the after-validator; no Alembic migration (the session is one JSON document, 0003).
design.offline: Entirely deterministic; no model involved. The model path only gains a truthful tool result.

designs.understanding: research/sources.py has one Cache class (Redis first, then disk) keyed on 'GET {url} {json(params)}' (sources.py:167). Because papers()/paper_count() put api_key into params, the key changes when OPENALEX_API_KEY is added or rotated. The disk layer writes in place (write_text) and json.loads with no error handling, so a torn file raises for up to 7 days. Disk hits are copied to Redis with the full TTL, doubling staleness. Only status 200 is cached, so EPO's 404 'no hits' repeats. There is no in-process single-flight, and the planned Redis lock (2.2.1) is 30 s against a 60 s client timeout with no re-check by waiters. core/redis.py remembers a failed ping for the life of the process. Warming (2.2.6) would key on registry phrasing nobody searches, share the whole daily cap with founders, and refetch entries still fresh. Reference dataset caches are ~25 independent lru_caches with hidden dependencies (get_ecosystem bakes in the banking branch index). Root cause: the cache has no defined key canonicalisation, entry envelope, write protocol, negative-result rule, concurrency rule or owner for dataset dependencies. All flags checked against current code.

approaches.basis: Popular asyncio cache libraries; cashews has 'locked' and 'early' (refresh-ahead) strategies.
approaches.advantages: Single-flight and refresh-ahead ready-made.
approaches.drawbacks: No disk backend without Redis in the default free setup (cashews needs an extra dependency for disk); keys built from function arguments bring back the credential problem unless customised; another layer to learn.

approaches.basis: Mature, widely used, pure Python.
approaches.advantages: Atomicity, TTL and multi-process safety solved by SQLite.
approaches.drawbacks: New dependency; the cache becomes an opaque SQLite file instead of inspectable JSON that the runbook and eval recordings use; does not address key canonicalisation, negative caching or warming policy.

approaches.basis: Postgres is already the system of record; advisory locks are a known single-flight tool.
approaches.advantages: Shared across workers without Redis; transactional.
approaches.drawbacks: Research must work when the database is down (the store falls back to memory); adds a migration and database load for a pure cache; contradicts SYSTEM-DESIGN section 4 (Redis then disk).

design.components: 1) backend/app/research/cache.py (new; Cache moved out of sources.py): canonical_key(), Entry envelope, DiskLayer (atomic), RedisLayer (remaining TTL), SingleFlight (in-process futures + optional RedisLock), fetch_cached(key, fetch, policy). 2) sources._get_json delegates to fetch_cached; per-source policies: cache 200 always; cache EPO 404 as empty with a 1-day negative TTL; never cache 429/5xx. 3) core/redis.py: a failed ping is remembered with retry_at (30 s, doubling to 5 min) instead of forever; is_live() for the status page. 4) research/requested.py: requested-keys index (Redis ZSET rs:req, or a disk JSON index when Redis is off) counting every founder lookup by canonical key with a replayable request spec. 5) scripts/warm_research_cache.py: refresh-ahead of requested keys with >= 2 requests whose remaining TTL < 24 h, charged to a separate warm budget share. 6) backend/app/core/datasets.py (new): @dataset_cache(name, reads=(...)) wrapping lru_cache and registering cache_clear with its dataset dependencies; clear_dataset(name) clears dependants transitively.
design.data_model: Entry = {v: 2, stored_at: epoch_s, status: 200|404, body}. canonical_key = 'v2 GET ' + url + ' ' + json(sorted params minus CREDENTIAL_PARAMS={'api_key','mailto','key','token','access_token'}), hashed with sha1 for file and Redis names. Disk file <hash>.json holds the Entry; old v1 files (bare body) are read with stored_at = mtime and expire naturally. Redis: rs:<hash> (Entry, ex = ttl - age), rs:lock:<hash> (redis-py Lock), budget:{source}:{date} (founders), budget:warm:{source}:{date} (warming), rs:req ZSET (canonical key -> request count) plus rs:req:spec:<hash>.
design.algorithm: fetch_cached(key): entry = Redis or disk; fresh if now - stored_at < ttl(status). Miss: if the key has an in-process future, await it. Otherwise create the future; if Redis is live, acquire Lock(rs:lock:<hash>, timeout = 3 x client timeout + 10 s (~190 s, papers makes three calls), blocking_timeout = 20 s). After acquiring (or after waiting), re-read the cache, then re-check pause and budget, then fetch. The holder writes the entry (200, or negative 404) and releases (Lock.release checks its token, so it cannot delete another holder's lock). On 429/5xx nothing is written; waiters see the pause key the holder set and return 'paused' without calling the source. Disk write: <hash>.json.tmp-<pid>-<rand>, fsync, os.replace; read: any OSError/JSONDecodeError/envelope mismatch -> log cache.corrupt(hash), unlink, miss. Disk-to-Redis copy uses ex = ttl - age (skip if <= 0). Warming: keys in rs:req by count, skip when remaining TTL > 24 h, stop when budget:warm reaches research_warm_share (default 25%) of the source limit or when the founder reserve would be touched; runs only between 22:00 and 05:00 IST.
design.interfaces: T33: canonical_key and Entry are the eval recording format (record = capture Entries per key; replay = serve them). T23: counters research.cache{layer=redis|disk|miss|negative|corrupt}, research.singleflight{joined}, gauge redis.live. Per-source budgets (another theme, F-B5-001) plug into the same budget check; the warm budget uses the same INCR helper. Reference-data reload (TASKS 2.2.3) calls clear_dataset(). T13: requested keys only ever contain allowlisted query words.

designs.understanding: Novelty statements (research/novelty.py _statement and levers) are chosen by which numbers happen to be present, not by what was actually searched. scan._local swallows every exception and returns the same {'startups': []} for 'error' and 'nothing found', with no coverage row, while novelty treats len(startups)==0 as 'no Tamil Nadu startup' even though the map covers only Chennai, Coimbatore and Madurai (654 records). The 'crowded' fallback fires when no pair was counted (one part, or every pair count failed). Query building takes the first content words from a public vocabulary that includes every word of every registry summary ('small', 'building', 'village'). scrub() is a denylist (drops a word only if the founder said it verbatim and it is not public), so brand variants pass. Two matchers over the same startup map (scan._local and cohort.reference.similar_startups) use different term rules and stoplists, so Talk and Cohort disagree. Root cause: no evidence ledger records search status and scope, statements are not gated on it, and term filtering and matching rules are duplicated. Flags checked; all hold.

Failing preconditions fall through to an honest 'unclear/not searched' template.
approaches.basis: Same pattern as decisions 0005 (fact check before speech) and 0006 (novelty from counts): code decides, templates word it.
approaches.advantages: Makes 'not searched is never nothing found' structural; easy to test; one table of claims.
approaches.drawbacks: Statements become more conditional; every caller must fill the ledger.

approaches.name: BM25 single matcher (rank-bm25) for local startups and cohort

approaches.basis: rank-bm25 is a small, popular pure-Python package; BM25 is the standard lexical relevance function.
approaches.advantages: Principled scoring, length normalisation, one function.
approaches.drawbacks: New dependency for 654 documents; BM25 score thresholds depend on the corpus; does not by itself fix the missing anchor-term rule or the coverage claim.

approaches.basis: Semantic matching catches synonyms.
approaches.advantages: Better recall on paraphrase.
approaches.drawbacks: pgvector is unavailable, the dependency and model download are heavy, and non-deterministic thresholds hurt eval reproducibility; goes against 'deterministic offline baseline first'.

approaches.basis: Decision 0004 already defines a public vocabulary; OpenAlex publishes its ~4,500 topics and keywords free; document frequency is the textbook way to find stopwords.
approaches.advantages: Brand variants cannot pass; filler words stop taking query slots; deterministic.
approaches.drawbacks: Some legitimate rare technical words are dropped (recall loss); the topic snapshot needs an occasional refresh.

designs.chosen: Evidence ledger + claim preconditions, combined with one shared IDF-anchored local matcher (stdlib, no BM25 package) and an allowlist query vocabulary with a document-frequency filter
designs.why_chosen: The theme has three causes and each chosen part fixes one at its root: the ledger makes every statement depend on what was searched (the honesty problem; the same M1 'typed outcome' pattern as T03/T28); one matcher module removes the Talk/Cohort contradiction by construction; and an allowlist with a DF filter enforces decision 0004 positively instead of hoping a denylist catches variants. All are deterministic and need no new runtime dependency (the topic list is a data snapshot).

design.components: 1) research/local.py (new): match_startups(text, sector=None, limit) -> LocalResult(status 'ok'|'not_searched'|'error', scope {source: 'TN Startup Map', districts, records, as_of}, items with shared terms). Uses planner.registry._terms stems, idf from the startup index, the FILLER stoplist from terms.py, and requires >= 2 shared terms of which >= 1 is an anchor with idf >= ANCHOR_IDF (about log(N/20)). The index is cached with T08's @dataset_cache('ecosystem'). 2) scan._local calls it and adds a 'local' coverage row; cohort.reference.similar_startups becomes a thin wrapper over the same function. 3) research/claims.py (new): a Ledger built in novelty.check from part counts, pair counts (with status), context counts and the LocalResult; a CLAIMS table [(type, precondition(ledger) -> bool, template)] evaluated in order, falling through to 'unclear'. Levers declare preconditions the same way. 4) research/terms.py: FILLER = words in more than DF_MAX (5%) of registry summaries plus a short curated list; query_vocabulary() = public vocabulary - FILLER; scrub() keeps a word only if it is in query_vocabulary or the technical allowlist (LEXICON terms, TERM_FIELDS, data/openalex_topics.txt), after normalising hyphenated, plural and split forms.
design.data_model: LocalResult {status, scope: {districts: [..], records: int, as_of: date}, items: [...]}. Ledger {parts: [{element, query, status, papers}], pairs: [{a, b, status, papers}], context: {status, world, india}, local: LocalResult}. Novelty output gains 'basis': {'pairs_counted': n, 'pairs_failed': m, 'local': status} so the client and T33 can check it. The scan coverage list gains {source: 'local', status, found, note: 'TN Startup Map: Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai (654 listed)'}.
design.algorithm: Statement order: combination gap (needs >= 1 pair with status ok and gap) -> context gap (needs context ok AND local ok; text '...and among the {records} startups the TN Startup Map lists for {districts}, I found none doing it') -> rarest element -> crowded (needs pairs_counted >= 1, pairs_failed == 0 and every part ok) -> unclear ('I could check only {k} of the parts; the combination was not counted'). Single-part ideas never reach 'crowded'; they get 'element' or 'unclear'. The localise lever needs local.status == ok and repeats the scoped wording. Matching: score = sum of idf of shared stems; accept when |shared - FILLER| >= 2 and max idf(shared) >= ANCHOR_IDF; the cohort count shown is the number accepted.
design.interfaces: T01: the sector filter uses canonical Sector values. T08: dataset_cache for the startup index; the requested-keys index only ever sees allowlisted queries. T28: novelty/evidence events carry the basis; the session stores the LocalResult so the Cohort page can read the same result by session id (POST /cohort/reference gains an optional session_id; ownership per T17). T33: degraded fixtures assert the 'unclear' and 'not searched' statements. T23: counter research.coverage{source,status}.
design.rollout: Ledger and claims first (the change is visible only in wording); then the shared matcher (re-record eval fixtures and compare counts on the 10 ideas); then the vocabulary change, measured with the eval set's paper totals before and after.
design.offline: Fully deterministic. With no network every remote status is not_searched, local is ok, and statements fall through to scoped local wording or 'unclear'. The topic snapshot is a file in the repo.

designs.understanding: Every page owns its own localStorage key and shape: journeyStore.ts and pages/Journey.tsx both write 'vanigam_journey' with incompatible shapes (versioned enums/consent/milestones vs unversioned {facts, done}), so each wipes or crashes the other. Keys are not scoped by user, and logout (auth.tsx:53-56) only clears tokens, so the profile (with caste category, phone, DOB), consent, pipeline, suppliers and the Talk session id survive for the next person on a shared device. Talk.tsx resumes with getSession(id).catch(() => save(null)), and agentClient's json() throws a bare Error for 404, 500 and network failure alike, so any transient failure throws away the only handle to the conversation (and to deleting it). Pipeline/Suppliers save whole arrays with Date.now() ids and no version, so syncing to the server (3.1.3) has no merge rule. Root cause: no registry of browser keys with an owner, a scope, a version/migration and a lifecycle, and no typed client error. Flags checked.

Logout and user change clear the scope; a CI grep forbids direct localStorage use elsewhere.
approaches.basis: The standard persistence pattern (redux-persist / zustand persist have version + migrate), written in ~120 lines without a framework.
approaches.advantages: Fixes collisions, leaks and migrations in one place; no runtime dependency; stays offline-first.
approaches.drawbacks: Every page's storage code changes; discipline is enforced by a grep check.

approaches.name: zustand with persist middleware
approaches.how: One zustand store per domain with persist({name, version, migrate, partialize}).
approaches.basis: Popular, small state library with built-in persistence and migration.
approaches.advantages: Versioning and migration ready-made; reactive across components.
approaches.drawbacks: New runtime dependency and a change of state style across pages that use useState today; user scoping and clear-on-logout are still ours.

approaches.name: IndexedDB via idb-keyval / Dexie
approaches.how: Move drafts to IndexedDB with per-user databases.
approaches.basis: Larger quota, structured storage; Dexie supports schema versions.
approaches.advantages: Quota and structure for future offline features.
approaches.drawbacks: The async API forces rewrites of synchronous loaders used during render; data volumes here are tiny; does not by itself define a merge or clearing policy.

approaches.name: Server as the only store (no browser persistence for signed-in users)
approaches.how: Signed-in pages read and write the server; localStorage only for anonymous drafts.
approaches.basis: SYSTEM-DESIGN rule 1: the server is the source of truth.
approaches.advantages: No cross-user leakage for signed-in users; no sync conflicts.
approaches.drawbacks: Breaks the offline/2G experience the product is built for; anonymous founders still need everything else.

approaches.name: Per-record version + updated_at with union-by-UUID merge (sync protocol)
approaches.how: Every list record gets a UUID, updated_at and version; the first sync unions by id; later writes use compare-and-set and a 409 on stale versions.
approaches.basis: The same optimistic concurrency as the session store (agents/store.py version check); last-writer-wins per record.
approaches.advantages: Two devices never erase each other's lists; reuses a pattern the backend already has.
approaches.drawbacks: Covers only sync; needs the registry to own ids and migrations.

designs.chosen: Typed key registry (scopes, versions, migrations, lifecycle) + typed ApiError in the client + per-record UUID/version sync protocol
designs.why_chosen: The registry is the missing owner: it ends the key collision, gives every record a migration instead of a silent discard, and makes clearing on logout or user change one loop. The typed ApiError (the same M1 'typed outcome' as T28's error codes) lets Talk forget a session only on a real 404 and offer delete on 'expired'. The record-level version/UUID protocol mirrors the session store's optimistic concurrency, so sync needs no new idea on the server. No new runtime dependency.

design.components: 1) frontend/src/storage/registry.ts: defineKey<T>({name, scope, version, empty, migrate, sensitive}); read/write/remove/subscribe (storage event for other tabs); currentOwner() from auth ('anon' or the user id); clearScope(owner); listKeys() for the privacy page. Registered keys: device scope: tokens, lang; user scope: profile, journey (v2), pipeline, suppliers, talk_session (+ the pending utterance queue from T28). 2) journeyStore.ts v2 absorbs Journey.tsx's registration {facts, done}; migrate() recognises v1 journeyStore records and unversioned {facts, done} records and merges both. 3) auth.tsx: logout -> clearScope(user) and clearScope('anon'); login -> if the anon scope holds data, ask 'Keep the drafts on this device for your account?' -> claim (copy into the user scope and call T17's claim for the talk session) or discard. 4) api/errors.ts: class ApiError {status, code, retryable, detail}; agentClient json() throws ApiError; network failures throw ApiError(status 0, code 'network', retryable). 5) Talk.tsx resume: 404 not_found -> forget; 404 expired -> keep the id and offer 'delete it' or 'start fresh'; 5xx/0 -> keep the id and show a retry notice with back-off. 6) Pipeline/Suppliers records: id = crypto.randomUUID(), updated_at, version; a migration rewrites 'local-<ts>' ids. 7) syncList(name): first sync = union by id, same id -> newer updated_at; later PUTs carry the version, the server answers 409 with its copy, and the client re-merges.
design.data_model: Stored envelope per key: {v: version, owner, updated_at, data}. Journey v2: {version: 2, entry_mode, reg_subtype, terrain, terrain_confirmed, consent, milestones, registration: {facts, done}}. List record: {id: uuid, updated_at: ISO, version: int, deleted?: bool (a tombstone, so a union does not bring deleted records back)}. Server records for sync (3.1.3) mirror this with a version column.
design.algorithm: read(key): parse the envelope; if v < version run the migrate chain; if migrate throws, keep the raw value under '<name>.bak' and return empty (never a silent loss). Merge on first sync: for each id in the union pick the record with the greater (updated_at, version); tombstones win over older live records. Logout: for each user-scope key, remove it for owners user and 'anon'.
design.interfaces: T17: the login claim uses the session claim operation and owner check; talk_session is user-scoped, so a new user never resumes another's conversation. T07: the backend distinguishes not_found from expired in the 404 body code. T28: ApiError codes are the same codes as the stream's typed error events; the utterance queue persists under talk_session. T03: toAgentProfile reads the profile through the registry. Generated TS types (T28, M4) give the server record shapes.
files: frontend/package.json (vitest dev dependency for registry and stream tests)
design.rollout: 1) The registry and migrations read the old key names (vanigam_journey etc.), so existing browsers keep their data, moved into the anon namespace on first load; 2) ApiError and the Talk resume policy; 3) the logout/login lifecycle; 4) the UUID record migration; 5) the sync protocol lands with 3.1.3. A CI grep fails if 'localStorage' appears outside storage/registry.ts.
design.offline: All local; works without a network. The retry notice appears only when the server is unreachable, and the session id is kept until a definite 404.

design.components: 1) core/metrics.py: Counter/Histogram registry; BUCKETS_MS log-scale 5..120000 (~20 buckets, x1.6); observe(name, ms, **labels) with a fixed label allowlist per metric (no ids, no text); snapshot_and_reset(); quantile(buckets, q). 2) core/metrics_flush.py: a lifespan task flushing every 60 s into metric_minute (Alembic migration), with 7-day retention. 3) core/middleware.py: RequestContextMiddleware rewritten as pure ASGI middleware wrapping send(): records time to http.response.start and to the final body chunk (more_body False) per route template; checks x-request-id against ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{8,64}$, else generates a uuid4 (the client value is never logged raw). 4) agents/ideation.py turn_stream: a TurnClock with perf_counter marks ack, first_sentence and done (and per tool call), observed as turn.ack_ms, turn.first_sentence_ms, turn.done_ms labelled by lane (offline/model/provider) and written as one 'turn.timing' log line. 5) agents/jobs.py: job.done with seconds; wait() counts job.wait{kind, outcome=in_time|late|failed}; a job duration histogram. 6) routers/status.py: GET /api/v1/status (operator token from settings, else localhost only): breakers (state, open_until), store name and database reachability, redis.is_live (T08), active research pauses (rs:neg keys or local pauses), budgets used, the model provider chain, 10-minute p50/p95 per metric, job in-time ratio. 7) Log policy: grounding.dropped logs problem codes and sha256(sentence)[:10]; a structlog processor truncates any string field over 200 chars and drops keys in a SENSITIVE_FIELDS set.
design.data_model: metric_minute(minute timestamptz, name text, labels jsonb (canonical, sorted), count bigint, sum_ms double precision, buckets int[], PRIMARY KEY (minute, name, labels)). Counters use count only. The flush reads the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and adds arrays in Python (volume is tiny), then upserts.
design.algorithm: p95 over a window: sum the bucket arrays, walk the cumulative counts to 0.95 x total, interpolate inside the bucket. Flush: swap the registry dicts (one event loop, so atomic), write the deltas; on a database error keep them and retry next minute (bounded to 60 minutes).
design.interfaces: T08: research.cache{layer}, research.singleflight, the redis.live gauge, budgets. T28: the TurnClock lives inside the typed event writer, so every emitted event can be timed; timings stay server-side. T03: elicitation.put{status}. T13: research.coverage{source,status}. The per-source budget theme (F-B5-001) reads its counters here. The frontend reports first-audio latency (TTS) with a small POST /api/v1/status/client-timing (bounded, no ids), observed as voice.first_audio_ms.
design.rollout: Log policy first (a privacy fix with no dependency). Then the registry and the in-process status page; then the database roll-up migration. Each metric is added by the theme that owns the code path, through the registry API.
design.offline: No external service. Without a database the status page shows this worker's in-process numbers and says so; without Redis it reports 'Redis: off'.

designs.understanding: The turn stream (routers/ideation.py agent_turn_stream) yields dicts built ad hoc by _event(kind, data) in agents/ideation.py, and the browser declares them again by hand (agentClient.ts AgentEvent). The session is saved only when 'done' is produced, and a VersionConflict at that point becomes an 'error' event after every sentence was already spoken under HTTP 200. The client loop (agentClient.ts streamTurn) treats end-of-body as success without checking that 'done' arrived. There is no client turn id, so a retry after a drop re-runs the turn; the planned idempotency (1.1.4) is on the non-stream route that the Talk page never calls. Notices go only to queues subscribed at that moment (jobs.py notify), and snapshot() reads s.scan etc., which only _absorb fills on the next turn. Talk.tsx keeps only the latest queued utterance. 20 of 49 OpenAPI operations (all agent routes) have no response schema. Root cause: the stream has no typed contract (event union, terminal sentinel, error codes, idempotency key, replay). Flags checked.

flags_disputed.note: Its last clause (an expired session silently dropped) is T18's resume policy and is resolved there; the replay half is resolved here.

approaches.name: Typed event union + turn claim/commit with client_turn_id + recorded last turn for replay
approaches.how: Pydantic discriminated union TurnEvent (ack, sentence{seq}, tool, evidence, novelty, council, done, error{code, retryable}); one TurnWriter writes the stream. Before the first event the server claims the turn (CAS save of {client_turn_id, at}); on completion it commits the session plus last_turn {client_turn_id, events} in one CAS save and only then emits done. A repeat of the same client_turn_id replays the recorded events; a conflict at claim returns a real HTTP 409 before anything is spoken.
approaches.basis: Optimistic concurrency already exists in the store (version check); idempotency keys are the standard pattern for retried POSTs; discriminated unions are first-class in Pydantic v2 and OpenAPI 3.1.
approaches.advantages: Fixes truncation, duplicates, late conflicts and the untyped OpenAPI with one contract; works for the stream and non-stream routes.
approaches.drawbacks: Two saves per turn (claim + commit); the session document grows by one turn's events.

approaches.name: WebSocket conversation channel
approaches.how: Replace SSE + POST with one WebSocket carrying typed messages both ways, with acks.
approaches.basis: Mature in FastAPI/Starlette.
approaches.advantages: Bidirectional, natural queueing and acks, one connection for turns and notices.
approaches.drawbacks: Large rewrite; proxies and 2G networks drop idle WebSockets; reconnection and replay must still be designed; idempotency is still needed.

approaches.name: sse-starlette with event ids and Last-Event-ID resume
approaches.how: Use sse-starlette's EventSourceResponse with ids; the client resumes a cut stream from the last id.
approaches.basis: Popular SSE helper for Starlette; Last-Event-ID is in the SSE standard.
approaches.advantages: Standard resume semantics, built-in ping.
approaches.drawbacks: The turn stream is a POST read with fetch, not EventSource, so Last-Event-ID is not automatic; resuming needs server-side buffering of in-flight events anyway; a dependency for formatting we do in one function.

approaches.name: Non-streaming turns with idempotency only (drop SSE for turns)
approaches.how: Use the JSON /turns route with an Idempotency-Key and a cached response; speak after the full reply arrives.
approaches.basis: Simplest correct HTTP semantics.
approaches.advantages: Real 409s, trivial retries.
approaches.drawbacks: Loses sentence-by-sentence speech, the main latency win for voice on slow models; contradicts the streaming voice design.

approaches.name: Client-side buffering only (speak after done)
approaches.how: Keep the protocol; the client buffers sentences until done arrives and discards them on error.
approaches.basis: No server change.
approaches.advantages: Never speaks a turn that failed.
approaches.drawbacks: The same latency loss as non-streaming; duplicates and replays stay unsolved.

designs.chosen: Typed TurnEvent union written by one TurnWriter, turn claim/commit keyed by client_turn_id with last-turn replay, typed error codes, notice replay on subscribe, a client utterance queue, and OpenAPI-to-TypeScript generation
designs.why_chosen: Claiming the turn before speaking moves conflicts to a real 409 at request time, which removes the 'spoken then discarded' case at its root instead of softening it; the recorded last turn gives idempotent retries on the route the Talk page actually uses; the terminal 'done'/'error' sentinel tells the client when to retry. One typed writer is also where T23's TurnClock sits, and the same Pydantic models are exported to TypeScript (M4), so Python and the browser cannot drift. Everything reuses the store's version check; no new runtime dependency.

design.components: 1) backend/app/agents/events.py (new): Pydantic models AckEvent, SentenceEvent{seq, text}, ToolEvent, EvidenceEvent, NoveltyEvent, CouncilEvent, DoneEvent{turn_id, reply, action, ...}, ErrorEvent{code: 'conflict'|'turn_in_progress'|'failed'|'not_found'|'expired', detail, retryable}; TurnEvent = Annotated[Union[...], Field(discriminator='event')]; a TurnWriter that serialises, numbers and times (T23 TurnClock) every event and records it. 2) AgentTurnIn gains client_turn_id: UUID (optional for compatibility; the server generates one when absent). 3) Router: load -> if last_turn.client_turn_id == id and committed -> replay the events (no model call); claim: s.turn_claim = {client_turn_id, at}; CAS save; VersionConflict -> HTTP 409 code conflict; a fresh claim with a different id -> 409 turn_in_progress (stale after 120 s); the same id -> takeover. Commit: s.last_turn = {client_turn_id, events, committed_at}; clear the claim; CAS save; then yield done. A disconnect before commit clears the claim in finally (best effort), and the next retry re-runs. The non-stream /turns route uses the same functions. 4) Notices: Board already keeps LATEST results; on subscribe send the latest result per kind with id '<kind>:<finished_at>'; the Last-Event-ID header (EventSource sends it on auto-reconnect) skips results already delivered. snapshot() merges board results newer than s.scan etc. 5) Client: streamTurn requires a terminal event, otherwise throws StreamCut (retryable); Talk retries up to 2 times with the same client_turn_id and back-off, and skips sentences whose seq was already spoken when the server replays (committed replays are identical). 6) Talk queue: an array of utterances, joined with ' ' into the next turn and each shown in the transcript; persisted in the talk_session registry key (T18). 7) Response models on all agent routes; the stream is documented as responses={200: {'content': {'text/event-stream': {'schema': TurnEvent}}}}; openapi-typescript (dev dependency) generates frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts; CI regenerates and diffs.
design.data_model: AgentSession gains turn_claim: {client_turn_id, at} | None and last_turn: {client_turn_id, events: [TurnEvent dicts], committed_at} | None (the latest turn only, ~2-10 KB). Both are stored in the session JSON (0003); old documents load with None.
design.algorithm: Client: id = crypto.randomUUID() per utterance (or per merged queue batch); attempt(n): stream; terminal done -> ok; error{retryable} or StreamCut with n < 2 -> wait 1 s x 2^n -> attempt(n+1) with the same id; error{conflict} -> reload the snapshot and say the fixed recorded phrase 'This conversation changed on another screen; I have reloaded it.' The server claim CAS keeps at most one live turn per session across processes; the in-process asyncio.Lock stays as a fast path.
design.interfaces: T27: the action in ack/done is the state machine's typed PendingAction model (same union approach). T07: CAS save and VersionConflict semantics come from the store contract; claim staleness uses its clock. T23: TurnWriter carries the TurnClock. T18: ApiError codes equal ErrorEvent codes; queued utterances persist in the registry. T03: done carries learned/conflict outcomes.
files: backend/app/agents/store.py (claim helpers on the existing version check)
design.rollout: Server first with client_turn_id optional, so the current client keeps working; then the client sends ids and checks the sentinel; then notice replay; then type generation with the CI diff. No database migration (session JSON).
design.offline: Pure protocol; the offline lane benefits equally. Replays need no model, so a retried turn costs no free-tier quota.

approaches.drawbacks: New dependency; matching on full URLs includes the api_key unless filtered; YAML cassettes duplicate what the cache Entry already is; failure injection for degraded paths is still custom.

files: backend/app/agents/tools.py (_roadmap keeps domain_card and risk labels)
design.rollout: Land the deterministic report and --check first (independent). Then HTTP recording after T08 task 1 (canonical key): re-record all 10 ideas once with the free sources and switch the runner, keeping the old fixture fields for one PR to diff scan output. Then the degraded profiles and the unscripted check (which fails until ideas.json gets dynamic answers).
design.offline: The eval runs with no network, no model and no Redis, as today; only recording needs the network (free sources, run by hand).

tasks.title: HTTP-boundary record and replay with the canonical key
tasks.why: Replaying the finished scan means the scan and novelty logic, and the categories check, test nothing.
tasks.where: backend/tests/eval/http_replay.py (new), runner.py, scripts/record_eval_fixtures.py, research/scan.py and novelty.py (client hook)
tasks.how: RecordingTransport/ReplayTransport keyed by research.cache.canonical_key; the runner injects the replay client and disables the cache; fixtures v2; unrecorded-request check; the categories check reads the live s.scan.
tasks.when: After T08 task 1 (canonical key and Entry).
tasks.what_for: A change to FIELD_TO_CATEGORY, the clinical filter or the domain fallback turns the quality set red.

subtasks.text: Record and replay raw HTTP entries; scan/novelty run for real in the eval; categories checked on the current output

tasks.title: Degradation profiles over the same recordings
tasks.why: No fixture exercises the 'papers not searched' or all-sources-down paths the free offline product depends on.
tasks.how: Transport profiles forcing 429/5xx/ConnectError per host; per-profile expectations in ideas.json; a matrix run in test_eval.py.
tasks.when: After task 1; the expectations use T13's honest statement types.
tasks.what_for: Degraded answers are held to the same quality bar as the normal path.

subtasks.text: openalex_down and all_down profiles with expectations on categories, statements and the absence of claims

tasks.title: Unscripted-question check and payer answers
tasks.why: The runner answers 'skip' to anything unscripted, so the payer question is skipped in all ten ideas without a failure.
tasks.how: Add answers.dynamic and allowed_skips per idea; a check fails when an asked slot has no scripted answer and may not be skipped.
tasks.when: Independent.
tasks.what_for: The most important answer path (customer and willingness to pay) is exercised, and new or irrelevant questions are caught.

subtasks.text: Unscripted-question check; dynamic payer answers for all ten ideas

tasks.title: Check the delivered roadmap, not a rebuilt plan
tasks.why: The eval rebuilds build_plan without the model's domain_id, so a wrong delivered roadmap passes.
tasks.how: s.roadmap keeps domain_card, pack and risk labels; the domain, pack, risk and milestone checks read s.roadmap only.
tasks.when: Independent.
tasks.what_for: When the model path is evaluated (5.1.2), a wrong domain_id fails the set.

subtasks.text: Store domain_card and risk labels on s.roadmap; the runner checks s.roadmap

tasks.title: Deterministic report with a --check mode in CI
tasks.why: The report embeds a run timestamp, so a regenerate-and-diff check always fails and gets dropped.
tasks.how: Replace 'Generated <now>' with the fixtures' recorded dates; stable ordering; --check compares the regenerated text with the committed file and exits non-zero on a difference; CI runs it.
tasks.when: First (independent).
tasks.what_for: The committed report always matches the runner.

subtasks.text: Deterministic header and --check mode wired into CI

designs.tests: Meta-tests: changing FIELD_TO_CATEGORY in a test makes the categories check fail; a replay with an unknown key makes the 'unrecorded requests' check fail; profile all_down -> no sentence claims 'crowded' or 'no Tamil Nadu startup'; an idea with an unanswered dynamic question fails the unscripted check; eval_report --check on an unchanged tree exits 0, and after editing report.md exits 1.
designs.risks: Re-recording needs the free live sources and spends some daily budget (10 ideas x ~15 requests): run by hand off-peak. Query-building changes (T13) invalidate keys and force a re-record; the unrecorded list makes the cause obvious. Fixture size grows; OpenAlex 'select' already trims bodies, and fixtures can be gzip-compressed if they exceed a few MB.
